portInfo.description: Port of Skjolden markets itself as a call at the head of Lustrafjord, on Norway’s longest ice-free fjord system about 205 km from the open sea. The port’s own one-page fact sheet (updated content captured this research turn) publishes a 127.5 m cruise pier with 12 m alongside, maximum LOA 400 m and draft 12 m, plus a 36 m tender pier and Haugsbukta anchorage about 600 m from the tender pier. Technical pages repeat the same LOA/draft envelope and note a 45 m charted clearance at an overhead line as a limiting dimension on the approach. Season framing mid-April to mid-October. Door GPS null.

gettingThere.distanceToCity: Fact sheet does not publish a surveyed walk-minute from pier to village centre this capture — gap. Port recommends roughly 10 h at port ≈ 9 h ashore for a full excursion programme; treat that as operational guidance, not a passenger walking survey.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Confirm cruise-pier vs tender/anchorage before timing walks.
